title: Ex-Conservative MP sues Liberal volunteer over alleged election campaign interference
summary: A former Conservative MP is suing a Liberal volunteer, accusing the man of creating fake websites in a "malicious" and "calculated" plan to interfere with his re-election prospects during the 2025…

image.caption: Former Conservative MP Ryan Williams lost his re-election bid last year. He is now seeking damages for what he alleges was an attempt at interference by a Liberal campaign volunteer. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics

A former Conservative MP is suing a Liberal volunteer, accusing the man of creating fake websites in a "malicious" and "calculated" plan to interfere with his re-election prospects during the 2025 campaign.
Defendant denies allegations, says lawsuit based on 'speculation'

One-time Bay of Quinte MP Ryan Williams alleges Steven Solarz — who had ties to the Liberal campaign that year — defamed him when he set up websites to make it appear like the Conservative camp was behind "deceptive" tactics.
Williams, who was elected in 2021, lost to Liberal candidate Chris Malette by 3,700 votes.

According to documents filed as part of the lawsuit, Williams alleges Solarz set up multiple websites associated with Malette's campaign. At least one of them, chrismalette.ca, redirected visitors to Williams's official campaign website, said his statement of claim.
Williams's case alleges Solarz was trying to create confusion and wanted the Conservative side to "be blamed, criticized or publicly associated with deceptive campaign tactics."

After the election, the former MP got a court order to compel the domain registration company GoDaddy and the Canadian Internet Registration Authority to disclose who was behind the websites. Solarz's name was on the domain registries, the documents show.

items: Liberal Chris Malette flips Bay of Quinte

blocks.text: "[Solarz's] conduct was intentional, malicious, high-handed and calculated to cause harm to Williams and to interfere with his campaign and electoral prospects," his claim says.

"The defendant's conduct occurred during an active federal election campaign in which Williams's public reputation, credibility and trustworthiness were central to his candidacy and electoral prospects."
Williams is seeking $1.5 million in damages.
The lawsuit was filed earlier this year but has recently nabbed local attention. None of the allegations have been proven in court.
Solarz denies allegations
Solarz denies all the allegations and in his statement of defence argues Williams's claims are based on "speculation" and "inference."

His lawyers have asked a judge to dismiss the matter, suggesting Williams's case is a strategic lawsuit against public participation (SLAPP) intended to interfere with Solarz's rights including freedom of expression.

In a statement through his lawyer, Solarz said he only got involved with the Liberal Party in 2025, ran for the nomination in March of that year and volunteered on Malette's campaign during the final two weeks of the campaign. He said he has no personal relationship with Malette.
"I welcome the opportunity to address Mr. Williams's claims in court," he said.
"I recognize that this has been an unfortunate situation. However, because the matter is before the courts, I am unable to comment further at this time."
Malette's office said he "unequivocally condemns the alleged actions and reiterates that this kind of behaviour has no place in our democratic process."
His office said the MP would not comment further while the matter is before the court.
Williams told CBC News he also lodged a complaint with election authorities.
Poilievre accuses Liberals of 'dirty trick'
During a news conference in Belleville, Ont., on Thursday, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre said it appears the Liberals played a "terrible, dirty trick."
Poilievre says Liberals might have played 'dirty trick' on former Conservative MP's campaign
"I hope that they answer for what happened here and that there is justice," the leader said.
"It should never be allowed to happen in our democracy. We welcome competitive elections that are hard fought, but there should not be this kind of fraudulent activity."
